media.title: The Pygmalion Effect, Growth Mindset, & Learning ft. Robert Rosenthal

timecodes.what: At kf_002.jpg (22.1s) (high-contrast dark-background stimulus / title frame), Trevor Ragan's recording states "- My name is Bob Rosenthal and I'm a just retired professor of many, many years, 20 years here, 37 years at Harvard before that," — providing spoken context for first-grade teacher leaning in warmly beside a randomly chosen 'Harvard bloomer' desk while holding the typed roster.

Mid-segment widescreen camera frame at kf_006.jpg (70.7s) as narration explains "based on a table of random numbers. - Half of the rats cages were labeled the smart rats, the other half of the cages were labeled the dumb rats.", clarifying key empirical findings in Rosenthal & Jacobson's Oak School random 'academic spurter' teacher-expectancy experiment.

Around kf_010.jpg (96.8s) (widescreen camera frame), commentary states "One thing I forgot to tell you is these rats in this study, they couldn't read. So this wasn't about like their mindsets and attitudes,", connecting the empirical results to broader cognitive and neural science.
